ai.description: The Black Rock Agama reaches 30 cm in length. It is grey-brown with a distinct black tail and throat. Males display bright yellow or orange dorsal spots during the breeding season.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Laudakia melanura* is best distinguished by its uniform, velvety black or dark grey coloration, lacking the prominent yellow or orange dorsal spots seen in other agamas.
ai.habitat: *Laudakia melanura* inhabits arid, rocky outcrops and boulder-strewn slopes within scrublands and dry deciduous forests, typically ranging from lowlands up to 2,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Black Rock Agama is a diurnal lizard that frequently basks on sun-drenched boulders, retreating into deep rock crevices when threatened by predators.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Laudakia melanura* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 2–4 eggs. Breeding occurs during the warmer months, generally from April to July.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Laudakia melanura* is found in the arid regions of northwestern India, primarily across Rajasthan and parts of Gujarat, typically inhabiting rocky outcrops.
